r: A rate rise changes what every house is worth, even though the house itself stays the same. Between March 2022 and July 2023, the Federal Reserve raised its policy rate from near zero to 5.25–5.5%. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate follows ten-year Treasury yields more closely than it follows Fed announcements, and it climbed from roughly 3% to above 7%. On a $400,000 loan, the monthly payment went from about $1,686 to $2,661, so buyers found that their borrowing power had shrunk by more than a third. At those payments, the old prices no longer pass affordability calculations. Owners with loans below 4% stayed put rather than give up those cheap loans, so fewer homes were listed. Sales stall before prices fall: US existing-home sales dropped to 4.09 million in 2023, the lowest since 1995. Credit keeps the housing market going, and higher rates ration it, so demand falls.
